newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen lifts wheat, flour prices at IMF's request.
newsitem.headline: Yemen lifts wheat, flour prices at IMF's request.

text.p: Yemen on Tuesday raised wheat and flour prices in line with recommendations by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, only a few hours after the oil ministry raised petrol prices over 31 percent.

A Yemeni official, who declined to be identified, said the government had decided to raise wheat and flour prices and also to grant public sector employees a 10 percent cost of living wage increase from July 1.
The wheat and flour price increase marks the third and final phase of an economic reform programme prescribed by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

"An extraordinary session of the Yemeni cabinet decided on Tuesday to raise the price of wheat to 770 rials ($6.10) for a 50 kg (110 lb) bag from 670 riyals, and the price of flour for a 50 kg bag to 900 rials from 790," the official told Reuters.
Earlier on Tuesday, Yemen's oil ministry raised the price of petrol over 31 percent to 25 rials a litre from 19 rials and lifted the price of kerosene to 13 rials a litre from seven.
A statement issued by the oil ministry said the new prices came into effect at midday (0900 GMT) on Tuesday.
Fuel oil used at power stations and cement factories was raised to 11 rials from seven a litre, while diesel remains at six rials a litre.
Since late Monday long queues of cars have built up in front of petrol stations in the capital Sanaa and some other cities.

Residents said some petrol stations had closed ahead of the increase so that they could sell their petrol stocks at the higher price. They said queues also formed as motorists, expecting the increase, tried to take advantage of the cheaper, old price.
When Yemen increased the price of petrol to 19 rials from 12 in January 1996, farmers and students took to the streets and blocked a major Sanaa-Aden highway in protest.
In 1995, riots erupted in the southern port city of Aden over the doubling of petrol prices.
